title: Secrets in the pipeline: vaults, federated identity and minimal scope

videos.script: Your pipeline signs every image it pushes. To do it, a stage reads a password from a file on the CI server. {{file}} Every branch that is pushed can read that file. And the password works until somebody changes it, which nobody ever does. {{forever}} This lesson gives that secret an end. First it moves into Vault, running in a container on your own machine. {{vault}} A policy lets one path be read and nothing else. A token made by hand dies after thirty seconds, and you watch it happen. {{expiry}} Then you remove the last stored credential. Your CI server signs a short statement about each run: this repository, this branch. Vault checks the signature and decides for itself. {{token}} A run of main gets the password. A run of any other branch is refused, and Vault says which claim did not match. {{refused}} That same exchange is how GitHub Actions reaches a cloud with no keys stored anywhere. You read its configuration line by line, and you learn which line people leave out. {{cloud}}
